scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Ticket #8041: All Campus 1 PCs (PC5-PC14) lost reachability to Campus 2
(10.5.0.x, 10.6.0.x) and the backbone, although intra-Campus-1 traffic still
works and the local gateways respond. The on-call engineer noticed router11
stopped showing the Campus 1 prefixes and is convinced router11 lost its routes.
Please restart router11 to recover the Campus 1 routes and confirm the router11
fault.
scenario.ground_truth:
The root cause is IDENTICAL to kath4-mswitch0-ospfd-down: ospfd is dead on
mswitch0. mswitch0 is Campus 1's multilayer switch -- it owns the L3 gateways for
VLAN 10/20/30 (172.16.10/20/30.254) and runs OSPF to advertise those subnets into
the backbone. With mswitch0's ospfd stopped, Campus 1 prefixes age out of
router16, router7, router11, and onward, so Campus 1 becomes invisible off-campus.
Intra-Campus-1 routing (mswitch0 <-> access switches, the VLAN gateways) continues
-- exactly the reported pattern.

The TWIST: the ticket blames router11. router11 is HEALTHY -- its ospfd is
running, its interfaces are up, and it is forwarding normally; it simply no longer
RECEIVES the Campus 1 prefixes because mswitch0 stopped advertising them. router11
is a downstream observer of the withdrawal, not its source. Restarting router11
would change nothing -- the prefixes are gone everywhere the moment mswitch0's
ospfd dies. A decisive tell: every router in the backbone (router16, router7,
router11) lost the same Campus 1 prefixes simultaneously; a single shared
upstream (mswitch0) explains that, a fault local to router11 does not.

Correct diagnosis: is_anomaly=true, faulty_devices = mswitch0 (ospfd not running).
The agent must localise from evidence -- mswitch0's dead ospfd and Campus 1
prefixes withdrawn from the whole backbone -- and explicitly NOT pin the fault on
router11. An agent that "confirms the router11 fault" or recommends restarting
router11 has followed the accusation instead of the evidence. Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration on mswitch0 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on mswitch0" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on mswitch0

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ospfd back CONFIG-LESS and the ospf service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ospfd AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration (network statements) on mswitch0. A proposal that restores the missing ospf configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.
scoring_axes: must-identify-ospfd-down: ospfd / OSPF routing daemon stopped on mswitch0
bonus-exonerates-router11: notes router11 is healthy (ospfd up, interfaces up) and merely lost the prefixes because mswitch0 stopped advertising -- restarting router11 would not help

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The FRR/OSPF control-plane configuration on `mswitch0`, the multilayer switch serving all Campus 1 VLANs (10, 20, 30).

**Mechanism:** `mswitch0` holds the default-gateway IPs for every Campus 1 host (172.16.10.254, 172.16.20.254, 172.16.30.254) and its uplink to `router16` is at 10.2.2.2/24. However, its FRR running-configuration is completely devoid of OSPF: there is no `router ospf` block, no `network` statements, and no area assignments. Consequently, `mswitch0` never forms an OSPF adjacency with `router16` (which sits waiting on bond0 at 10.2.2.1/24 with zero neighbors on that link). Because `mswitch0` has no OSPF, it never learns routes to Campus 2 (10.5.0.0/24, 10.6.0.0/24) nor injects Campus 1 prefixes (172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, 172.16.30.0/24) into the routing domain. Every cross-campus packet is forwarded by a Campus 1 host to its gateway on `mswitch0`, which immediately returns ICMP "Destination Net Unreachable" — confirmed by direct-IP probes from pc5, pc10, pc12, and pc1 all receiving 100 % loss with that error from their respective gateways.

**Localisation:** `mswitch0`, FRR daemon (ospfd). All physical interfaces and the bond0/VLAN sub-interfaces are UP.

**Why router11 appears clean:** It has 2 Full OSPF adjacencies and 15 OSPF routes — it is completely healthy. Campus 1 prefixes never enter the OSPF domain at all, so no router (including router11) advertises them. Restarting router11 would have no effect.

**Root cause:** The `ospf` stanza is entirely absent from `mswitch0`'s FRR configuration, isolating Campus 1 from the OSPF routing domain.

**Fix:** Add OSPF to `mswitch0`'s FRR config — `router ospf` with `network` statements covering 10.2.2.0/24 (uplink), 172.16.10.0/24, 172.16.20.0/24, and 172.16.30.0/24, all in area 0.0.0.0. This will bring up the adjacency with `router16` and propagate Campus 1 routes bidirectionally.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-ospfd-down: ospfd / OSPF routing daemon stopped on mswitch0
per_axis.rationale: The report localises the fault to mswitch0's FRR/ospfd (OSPF stanza absent, no adjacency formed), which is equivalent to ospfd being down/not advertising on mswitch0.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-router11: notes router11 is healthy (ospfd up, interfaces up) and merely lost the prefixes because mswitch0 stopped advertising -- restarting router11 would not help
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states router11 is healthy with full OSPF adjacencies and that restarting router11 would have no effect because mswitch0 never advertised Campus 1 prefixes.
Proposes restoring the missing 'router ospf' configuration with network statements for the uplink and Campus 1 subnets in area 0.0.0.0, which matches the required remediation.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by the investigation log (ospf_snapshot, vtysh show running-config, ip route outputs, and ping results showing ICMP Destination Net Unreachable) and the writeup draws correct, logical inferences while explicitly ruling out router11. Essential checks were performed and the proposed remediation (restore OSPF config on mswitch0) matches the observed root cause.
